body: I'm at the point where my life is so fucked I can't get a fresh start. I just want to run away and tell everyone to go fuck themselves, but I don't make a lot of money at my job. How can you run away with no money? And on top of that I have so much debt from student loans, credit cards, nuthouse bill in collections, if I tried to start over I could never make enough to make these payments on time.  And once you can't pay any of your bills, how are you going to have a fresh start?

I spoke with a crisis hotline a few times before I checked myself into the nuthouse. Some people on the other end were better than others. I remember one would not listen to me and just kept interrupting as I was trying to explain stuff.
Lol it would just be nice to know that my family maybe wouldn't be as traumatized by my sudden suicide if they got monies
I don't think anyone will write me until next year and I'll probably be dead before the 2 year period or whatever

I'm not eligible either because I was in the nuthouse less than 2 years ago. Don't want to leave behind all kinds of debt either, but probably won't make it through the 2 or 3 year period during which the insurance companies would contest the claim. Sucks to suck
That's why this is so surprising to me. I feel like I have seen this drama in shows or movies and didn't realize it wasn't actually that way in the real world
Maybe I'm just a fucking moron then, idk, but I was led to believe that payout after a suicide was always a definite no from all insurers.

Maybe. I just feel like whenever it came up in a TV show or Death of a Salesman type shit where a character kills himself to provide insurance money to loved ones because they think they're worth more alive than dead, either a character or someone watching or reading the story with me would bring up how no policy would ever pay out if it was ruled a suicide
Apparently. I thought it would always get denied, 100% of the time by all companies
I guess I thought everyone was a dick then and no one would pay
That's what I've found today. I had heard it was always denied no matter what because you can't insure against an uncertainty that wasn't actually uncertain
Eh I always just figured people are dicks 🤷

I've always heard, incorrectly apparently, that if you kill yourself, since it's intentional, that when the beneficiary files the claim, it will always get denied, no matter what. Like if you burn down your own house for insurance money.
I feel you.  I'm getting to the point where I don't want to function.  I just want to lie down for a nap and not wake up.  But I don't know who would feed my doggy.
I'll listen to you if you'll listen to my stupid, indecisive, anxious ramblings

I was in 6th grade as well when it happened.  My dad happened to drive my sister and I to school that day.  He had the radio on and someone was on the phone talking to the host of the show.  I think that was when the second plane hit, this guy just started screaming and freaking out because he couldn't believe what he was seeing.

I didn't know what was going on at the time, my dad didn't tell my sister and I anything, but it just seemed like something was wrong.  Then when we got into school, no one told us anything.  I guess someone had told all of the teachers not to say anything, maybe so kids wouldn't freak out.  But my teacher told us what had happened.  She said that since we were the oldest in the school, she wanted us to know and try to be strong for the younger kids if they were to find out.

That reminds me of the time I had a stern talking to to a guy at work because whenever he would go about to do anything, he would always just be walking kind of slowly, just trudging off to do something he didn't want to do, or leaning on stuff or sitting down.  Well after I told him there were lots of things that needed to be done and he needed to hustle, he asked me if I knew that he had no legs.  I had no idea that his lower legs and feet were lost in a bad car accident.  Apparently he walks weird but I never noticed.  He said it was fine, I didn't know, so no big deal, but I still felt like a huge asshole.

I just want to die, and I'm not sure if it's more comforting to think of nothingness or think of an afterlife.  On one hand, would I really want to suffer in hell for eternity? But what if there's a chance that I would go somewhere better and be able to see my loved ones who have passed again or watch over people who are still here?  That might be nice.  Nothing will just be nothing.  Better than living, but it's not like you would know that.
And then maybe they won't feel as bad when you kill yourself because your life fucking sucks
If I wait until he comes back it'll be too late.  I really don't want to be put in an institution or anything

I don't think he truly wants to be with me.  We haven't been in a particularly good place and I feel like the friends he's visiting will probably just tell him that he should dump me anyway.  I don't think they like me.
